This World Cancer Day, let’s help find cures to childhood cancer.
Happy 64th birthday, St. Jude!

On World Cancer Day, St. Jude celebrates the work underway through the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines to coordinate national efforts to strengthen childhood cancer care and expand consistent access to treatment for children and families. 

In Ecuador, leaders are building more unified pathways for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care. Participation in the pilot phase of the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines, launched in 12 countries by St. Jude in collaboration with World Health Organization in 2025, has helped bring together institutions to establish shared approaches to care grounded in evidence. 

Progress includes receiving the first shipment of childhood cancer medicines through the Global Platform in the Americas, updating essential medicine lists and developing a national childhood cancer registry that will follow each child’s path from first symptoms through treatment and survivorship. These efforts help identify barriers and guide improvements. 

“For the first time, we will truly understand how children are moving through the system. We will see where they start, where they get stuck and where we need to improve,” said Lissette Mármol, MD, childhood cancer focal point at Ecuador’s Ministry of Public Health. 

As these efforts build momentum, they reflect the long-standing commitment that has guided St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital since its founding on February 4, 1962, to improve the way the world understands, treats and supports children with cancer. 

#WorldCancerDay

Meet St. Jude patient Isaac 👋

Isaac was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in March 2025 after his parents took him to a local hospital for what they thought was a lingering virus.

He was referred to St. Jude where doctors offered Isaac’s family a sense of calm and reassurance.

“They told me ‘We got you, everything is going to be fine. This is your team, and we have a plan,’ and that made me feel good,” his mom, Andrea, recalled. ❤️‍🩹

As Isaac's treatment continues, we are thankful for him and his family sharing their experience with St. Jude on the @todayshow.
